title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 135
paragraphs: Miltiades, then, in a wretched state, set out to sail home, bringing no wealth to the Athenians and having failed to add Paros to their possessions, but having besieged the city for twenty-six days and laid waste the island. The Parians, learning that Timo the under-priestess of the goddesses had guided Miltiades, wanted to take revenge on her, and as soon as they had leisure after the siege they sent messengers to Delphi to consult the god. They asked whether they should put to death the under-priestess of the goddesses, who had been a guide to their enemies for the capture of her native city and had revealed to Miltiades mysteries that must not be uttered to any male. The Pythian prophetess forbade them, saying that Timo was not truly the author of these events: since it was destined that Miltiades should come to a bad end, she had appeared to him in order to lead him to his destruction.
